9630a193ff10a1a610065f6bdc57a05e1c39d423: The 'Formigal-Panticosa' lift pass is shared with <t1>Panticosa</t1>: one ticket gives access to both ski areas, a combined 182 km of runs. The two resorts are not, however, linked by skis, so you have to drive between them. The distances and runs shown here relate to Formigal only. Formigal is the main resort of the Tena Valley, in the municipality of Sallent de Gállego, in the Aragonese Pyrenees. Opened in 1965, it spreads between 1510 and 2265 m over four valleys (Sextas, Izas, Anayet and Portalet), the latter sector reaching the French border at the col du Pourtalet. A large, varied ski area geared more towards confident skiers, with 36 black runs, it is also known for its lively après-ski at the foot of the slopes.

96478c6a18b8fb18d7a98d3b4fcf488c4a905552: The 123 km, 47 lifts and lift pass shown are those of the 4-Berge-Skischaukel ski area, shared by Schladming, Haus im Ennstal and Pichl – Reiteralm. Part of the Ski amadé network: multi-day Ski amadé passes also give access to the other ski areas in the network, which are not linked to one another, including <t1>Flachau</t1>, <t2>Zauchensee</t2>, <t3>Bad Gastein</t3>, <t4>Maria Alm</t4> and <t5>Schladming</t5>. The piste breakdown is given as a percentage of the kilometres for each difficulty level. Haus im Ennstal gives access to the Hauser Kaibling, which is linked to the Planai and the rest of the 4-Berge-Skischaukel. The village co-hosted the 1982 World Championships.
965defac40035f30cc034e32a424816b22d11115: The Gerlos ski area, with its 150 km of runs, offers a strong choice for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 52 lifts make it easy to link descents without long queues. Gerlos has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, unspoilt scenery and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialised skiing of some large ski areas. With a summit at 2500 m and a village at 1245 m, snow reliability at Gerlos is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strain early in the season, but conditions recover quickly with the first serious snowfalls. The budget for a stay in Gerlos is clearly high: 82€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but it's worth knowing before you go. In short: Gerlos keeps its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most skiers without disappointing.
